question: According to a Commission report entitled ‘Review of ongoing financial assistance to Palestine’1, in April 2023, social allowances were paid to a total of 106 596 families, 70 108 of which were supported by PEGASE. Given the level of poverty, the vast majority (73 %) of the beneficiary families were in Gaza.

According to data from the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD), 91 261 families were living in extreme poverty, 41 266 were headed by a woman, 16 395 were headed by a person with a disability and 42 130 were headed by an elderly person. 1.

How many beneficiaries in the Palestinian territories have received such social allowances from the EU budget in the last 10 years, broken down by year, and how much money in total was transferred annually for those social allowances?

How many beneficiaries in the EU have received such social allowances from the EU budget in the last 10 years, broken down by year, and how much money in total was transferred annually for those social allowances?

How many beneficiaries outside the EU and the Palestinian territories have received such social allowances from the EU budget in the last 10 years, broken down by year, how much money in total was transferred annually for those social allowances, and in which countries were the beneficiaries?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) The EU supports the Palestinian Authority (PA) in providing social allowances to vulnerable families under the Cash-Transfer Programme (CTP) through the Palestinian-European SocioEconomic Management and Assistance Mechanism (PEGASE). This is crucial for the socioeconomic stability of the occupied Palestinian territory.

Between 2016 and 2024, the EU transferred via PEGASE EUR 356 923 007 in total to Palestinian households, as per the table in annex. All financial support under PEGASE is subject to strong ex-ante and ex-post controls and safeguards to ensure that EU funds are issued only for intended purposes.

The EU applies a strict vetting process to beneficiaries of its payments and tracks the financial transfer to each vetted individual. Since 2024, the EU is supporting the PA in reforming its social protection system.

In February 2025, the Presidential Decree 4/20251 established a single unified framework under the Palestinian National Foundation for Economic Empowerment PNEEI (or ‘Tamkeen’), which is now responsible for the CTP.

The Commission has launched a detailed audit of this new system and will disburse funds under the CTP only once it has received all reassurances that the new system is effective for the sound transfer of funds under that programme. EU funds transferred via PEGASE do not support Palestinian households residing outside the occupied Palestinian territory.
